title: Missing data and cluster graphs: cluster-level missingness vs variable-level missingness
claim: Multiple distinct fine-grained causal graphs can be compatible with the same coarse cluster-level graph, so abstraction loses structural detail.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, labeled (a)(b)(c), two detailed graphs beside one abstract graph
description: Three side-by-side directed graph diagrams drawn in black and white with circular nodes and arrows, labeled (a), (b) and (c). Panels (a) and (b) each show six variable nodes in a two-row grid, Z1, X1, Y1 on the bottom and Z2, X2, Y2 on top. The two panels differ in their edges. For example, (a) has Z1→X2 and X1→Z2, while (b) has X2→Z1 and Z2→X1, plus X2→Y2 and X1→Y1. Panel (c) is a compact chain of three cluster nodes, C_Z, C_X and C_Y, with a bidirected pair of arrows between C_Z and C_X and a single arrow from C_X to C_Y. The eye goes to the crossing arrows in (a) and (b) first, then to the simpler graph in (c) that summarizes both. There is no color or other decoration.
caption: Two ADMGs in (a) and (b) compatible with the same C-DMG in (c).
abstract: Missing data is pervasive in many scientific domains such as public health, environmental science, and the social sciences. Recoverability from missing data is typically studied using fully specified variable-level missingness models despite that, in many applications, only coarse structural information is available, for instance when variables are grouped into clusters due to limited knowledge or interpretability reasons. In this paper, we investigate recoverability from such abstract representations. We introduce two classes of cluster-based missingness graphs: the m-C-DMG, which retains variable-specific missingness indicators, and the cm-C-DMG, which aggregates missingness mechanisms at the cluster level. We formalize the notion of compatibility between these abstract graphs and underlying variable-level missingness models, and study how this abstraction affects the recoverability of probabilistic and causal queries. In particular, we give graphical conditions of recovering the joint distribution as well as graphical conditions of recovering a macro causal effect.
